speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your fatigue and severe itching, do you have any dark urine or pale stools, and have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, I need to rule out primary sclerosing cholangitis, but your sexual history also raises concern for viral hepatitis. Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, and have you experienced any right upper quadrant abdominal pain or jaundice?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and current signs of cholestasis, I need to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: MRCP of the liver and biliary tree.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP is normal, Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis is unlikely, so I need to evaluate other causes of cholestasis. Do you have any history of autoimmune diseases, and have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools? REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune hepatitis panel, ANA, SMA, and AMA.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Autoimmune hepatitis panel: Negative, ANA: Negative, AMA: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: With PSC, autoimmune hepatitis, and primary biliary cholangitis effectively ruled out by the negative imaging and serology, I suspect a viral etiology given your sexual history. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C antibody, and HIV viral load.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative viral and autoimmune workup, I need to investigate other causes of cholestasis or metabolic liver disease. Do you have a history of alcohol use, and have you experienced any unintentional weight loss or fever? REQUEST TEST: Serum ceruloplasmin, serum iron studies, and alpha-1 antitrypsin level.

speaker: Doctor
text: With metabolic, viral, and autoimmune causes ruled out, I need to consider drug-induced liver injury or other cholestatic conditions. Have you been taking any new medications, supplements, or herbal remedies recently? REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and coagulation profile.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 11.5 g/dL, Leukocyte_Count: 7500/mm3, Platelet_Count: 280,000/mm3, Na: 138 mEq/L, K: 4.7 mEq/L, Bilirubin_Total: 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 460 U/L, AST: 75 U/L, ALT: 78 U/L

speaker: Doctor
text: Your lab results show a cholestatic pattern with significantly elevated alkaline phosphatase, but since common causes have been ruled out, I need to look deeper. I will order an abdominal ultrasound to check for any structural abnormalities in the liver or bile ducts. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of bile duct thickening and dilatation are highly suggestive of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, despite the initial normal MRCP. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
